scope: Lens extraction only. Do not fix pre-existing gateway problems, change unrelated CI policy, or upgrade dependency/tool versions. The Grype version matches the existing gateway scanner.

findings.detail: No official Lens release exists. Both host chart publishers must consume the signed selected Lens release before a gateway chart can publish. Combined source selection and artifact wiring remain required; no registry publication was performed.

Source charts contain development defaults, Lens remains disabled by default, and source installation guides require a built image. Official release packaging must select the Lens release version and digest.

pip install . does not compile the dashboard. Contributor guide now identifies npm ci and build_ui.sh to refresh local output. Official images and wheels use the release UI build. No generated legacy bundle is replaced in source.
Both token verifiers permit issued-at up to five seconds ahead. Expired tokens, lifetime over 60 seconds, zero/negative lifetime, wrong signatures and wrong scope remain rejected.
Delegated Lens identity now uses the same permitted-team lookup and own-user fallback as native gateway traces. Administrators avoid permission database lookup; failed lookup never broadens access.

Standalone and both host charts generate distinct signing and service secrets, preserve them on Helm upgrade, and require both external references. Canonical docs and host chart READMEs document the distinction.

Lens paths leave the inference group. Lens still authorizes delegated users, including viewer POST reads. enforce_user_param continues to reject inference requests without user while allowing Lens management requests.

No current field mismatch exists. Rejecting unknown authenticated claims is intentional. A future identity schema change requires compatibility qualification and a contract version change where needed; accepting unknown claims is not a fix for a current regression.

findings.disposition: fixed gate, final candidate scan still required
findings.detail: Both Lens native container CI lanes and publisher-owned native staging now scan for fixable high/critical findings before staging. Reports are retained even on failure; no package upgrade or custom advisory suppression was added.

PostgreSQL rows are preserved. The packaged lens-migrate path and populated migration/recovery receipts already exist. Actual installation must stop writers and migrate before switching; no runtime compatibility layer was added.

Request and response buffers are capped at 64 MiB, but that is a per-call cap. Aggregate forwarding memory still needs qualification or a Lens-only resource bound before final readiness. No arbitrary lower data limit or unrelated gateway throttle was introduced.

Offline rendering cannot reuse lookup-generated credentials. The Helm guide now requires preprovisioned references and external supported ClickHouse for this path; it does not claim random output is deterministic.

findings.disposition: informational, not an independent trust anchor
findings.detail: The configured public key is the trust root; a checksum stored alongside it detects accidental mismatch only. Repository settings access is trusted, and the artifact-provided key is not accepted as authority. No trust-policy weakening was made.
